specPoints.text: understand the roles of oestrogen and progesterone in the menstrual cycle

primer.text: Twenty-eight days, two ovarian hormones, one repeating script. Oestrogen climbs first, thickening the uterine wall and peaking just before the egg's release; progesterone takes the second half, finishing the lining and then collapsing to start the period. This note maps both hormones onto the cycle's calendar.

lessons.title: The Cycle's Calendar
lessons.opening: The menstrual cycle starts at puberty and runs about 28 days: the lining builds toward ovulation around day 14, and if no fertilisation happens the endometrium sheds as menstruation before thickening again for the next round.
keyPoints: The average cycle lasts about 28 days, though it varies between individuals.
Ovulation occurs around day 14, releasing an egg that travels toward the uterus.
If no fertilisation happens, the uterine lining breaks down and sheds as menstruation.
Menstruation runs about 5 to 7 days and opens the next cycle.
Once menstruation ends, the lining rebuilds ahead of a possible implantation.

low.restatement: Build the lining, release the egg at day 14, and if nothing implants, shed the lining and restart.
low.analogy: Monthly redecorating of a spare room: prepare it, wait, then clear it out if no guest arrives.
low.examPointer: Quote day 14 for ovulation and 5 to 7 days for menstruation — the numbers anchor the marks.

medium.restatement: The calendar is hormone-written: the lining's rebuild after menstruation sets the stage, the mid-cycle egg release offers fertilisation its window, and the absence of pregnancy resets the whole sequence through shedding.
medium.analogy: A theatre that rebuilds the set each act for a star who may never arrive.
medium.examPointer: Name the endometrium as the uterine lining that breaks down — the term earns recognition.

check.stem: How long is the average menstrual cycle?

options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
Seven days matches a period's length, not the full cycle.
Fourteen days is the ovulation midpoint, not the cycle.
The cycle is far shorter than ninety days.

check.stem: Around which day does ovulation occur in a 28-day cycle?

options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Day 1 marks menstruation's start.
Day 7 is still lining rebuild, not egg release.
Day 28 is the pre-menstrual end of the cycle.

check.stem: What happens to the uterine lining if the egg is not fertilised?

options.text: It breaks down and sheds away through the vagina as menstruation
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
The lining sheds without pregnancy.
The placenta forms from implantation tissue, not the shed lining.

options.text: It stores the egg for next month
options.explanation: A new egg matures next cycle; the lining does not store it.

check.stem: How long does menstruation usually last?

options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
That is the fertilisation window, not the period.
Half the cycle is not spent menstruating.
The period is much shorter than twenty days.

check.stem: After menstruation ends, what prepares the uterus for a possible pregnancy?

options.text: Hormones make the lining thicken again for the next cycle
options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.

options.text: The lining is shed a second time
options.explanation: One shed per cycle; rebuilding follows.
The next egg matures first; implantation needs fertilisation.
The cycle repeats monthly after puberty begins.

check.stem: State the name for the breakdown and shedding of the uterine lining.
check.modelAnswer: The breakdown and shedding of the uterine lining is called menstruation.

check.stem: State the day on which an egg is released and the tube it travels along.
check.modelAnswer: An egg is released around day 14 and rides the fallopian tube toward the uterus.

check.stem: Explain why the uterine lining thickens before ovulation rather than after menstruation only.
check.modelAnswer: The rebuilt lining is the landing site a fertilised egg would need, so it must be ready by the time the day-14 egg could implant.

check.stem: A tracker app logs a user's period starting on day 1. On which cycle day should it predict ovulation for a 28-day rhythm?
check.modelAnswer: The app should predict ovulation around day 14, the midpoint of the 28-day cycle.

lessons.title: Oestrogen and Progesterone in Charge
sourceHeadings: Hormonal control of the menstrual cycle
lessons.opening: Oestrogen writes the first half of the cycle: it climbs from day 1, thickening the uterine wall and maturing the egg until its peak just before release. Progesterone writes the second half: low until ovulation, then rising to hold the lining, and its fall is the period's starting gun.
keyPoints: Oestrogen levels rise from day 1 and peak just before day 14.
Rising oestrogen thickens the uterine wall and matures the egg as day 14 approaches.
Progesterone stays low from day 1 to 14 and rises after ovulation has occurred.
Rising progesterone causes the uterine lining to thicken further.
A fall in progesterone causes the lining to break down as menstruation.

low.restatement: Oestrogen builds first and peaks mid-cycle; progesterone finishes the job and its drop starts the period.
low.analogy: Two decorators on shifts: the first prepares the room, the second finishes it, and their stopping time signals clearing day.
low.examPointer: Tie each hormone to its half of the cycle and to the lining's fate.

medium.restatement: The two hormones divide the calendar precisely: oestrogen's climb pairs lining growth with egg maturation so both peak together, and progesterone's post-ovulation rise sustains what oestrogen began until its collapse withdraws the lining's support.
medium.analogy: A relay where the baton passes at day 14 and the second runner's slowdown ends the race.
medium.examPointer: Quote the progesterone fall as the trigger for menstruation — that causal link scores.

options.text: Just before day 14, right before the egg is released
options.explanation: Correct — this follows directly from the definition.
The peak sits mid-cycle, not at the end.
Oestrogen starts low at day 1 and climbs.
The second half belongs to progesterone.

check.stem: What does rising oestrogen do before ovulation?

options.text: It starts the uterine wall thickening and the egg maturing
options.explanation: Yes — the mechanism works exactly this way.
Shedding follows progesterone's fall.
Menstruation is not oestrogen's doing.

options.text: It releases progesterone from the pituitary
options.explanation: Progesterone is ovarian and rises later.

check.stem: When does progesterone begin to rise?

options.text: After ovulation has occurred, around day 14
options.explanation: Correct — this matches the account taught above.
Progesterone stays low in the first half.
It falls at menstruation; it does not rise then.
The rise follows ovulation, not precedes it.

check.stem: What does increasing progesterone do to the uterine lining?

options.text: It causes the lining to thicken further and stay maintained
options.explanation: Right — this is the account the lesson teaches.
The breakdown follows progesterone's fall.
Shedding is what progesterone prevents.

options.text: It has no effect on the lining
options.explanation: Maintaining the lining is its core role.

check.stem: A drop in which hormone starts menstruation?

options.explanation: Right — the other options each misplace a concept.
Oestrogen peaks mid-cycle; its drop is not the period trigger.
FSH rises early for follicle maturation.
LH causes ovulation; the period follows progesterone's fall.

check.stem: State the hormone that stays low for the first 14 days of the cycle.
check.modelAnswer: Progesterone stays low from day 1 to 14 and climbs after ovulation.

check.stem: State the two effects of rising oestrogen before the egg is released.
check.modelAnswer: Oestrogen causes the uterine wall to thicken and the egg to mature.

check.stem: Explain why a fall in progesterone leads to menstruation.
check.modelAnswer: Progesterone maintains the thickened uterine lining, so when its levels fall the lining loses that support and breaks down as menstruation.

check.stem: A hormone test on day 20 shows high progesterone. What does this indicate about the cycle stage and the lining?
check.modelAnswer: Day 20 sits after ovulation, so high progesterone shows the second half of the cycle is under way and the uterine lining is thickened and maintained.

glossary.definition: The roughly 28-day repeating cycle in which the uterine lining builds and sheds.
The release of an egg from an ovary, around day 14 of the cycle.
The ovarian hormone that rises to a peak just before day 14 and thickens the uterine wall.
The ovarian hormone that rises after ovulation and maintains the uterine lining.
